sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Western blot on HEK293T cell lysates confirmed expression of the HA-tagged construct; no surface localisation assay or functional assay reported.
sites.rationale: L1 reports an N-terminal HA tag on full-length, membrane-anchored Fam171a1; no residue number is given, but FAM171A1 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–21 and a single extracellular N-terminus beginning at residue 22. An N-terminal tag upstream of the signal peptide would be cleaved off, so the only valid extracellular placement is after the signal peptide cleavage site, i.e. insert_after_residue = 21 (junction T|K). Python confirmed residue 21 = T and residue 22 = K, consistent with the canonical sequence. The tag junction sits 282 residues from the TM boundary (304), well clear of any constraint. Full-length Fam171a1 expressed with an N-terminal HA epitope tag in HEK293T cells; expression confirmed by western blot on cell lysates. No specific residue number is named in the paper.

sources.claim: We analyzed their specificity on lysates of HEK293T cells that were transfected with all three Fam171 family members (Fam171a1, Fam171a2 and Fam171b), containing an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) epitope tag ( Figure 1B ).

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) exists for FAM171A1. It reports a full-length, membrane-anchored construct with an N-terminal HA tag confirmed by western blot in HEK293T cells. No residue number is stated, but the signal peptide (1–21) leaves exactly one extracellular N-terminus (residue 22), so the junction is topology-derived at insert_after_residue = 21. No loop-internal insertions, no intracellular tags, and no function-abrogating positions are mentioned anywhere in the ledger, so other_positions is empty. Validation is detected_only because only a western blot (lysate) is reported — no surface staining, flow cytometry, or functional assay is described.
